requirements.statement: A maintained build derives all configuration and targets from one effective configuration bundle and fails on missing, unknown, contradictory or stale inputs.
requirements.acceptance: Reconfigure maintained presets and external consumers; invalid symbols, stale generated bundles and target/config disagreement fail before artifact acceptance. Record actual nonzero checks against the same source and configuration.

requirements.statement: Typed device and component contracts preserve owner/generation identity, explicit capability and caller buffer leases through completion, cancellation, provider faults and recovery.
requirements.acceptance: Production caller tests reject stale references and duplicate completion, retain unsettled buffers and bounded callback contexts, and exercise FULL retry and teardown failures. Unsupported MCU providers remain explicit; any hardware lease or DMA qualification requires named-board execution evidence.

requirements.statement: OSAL and infrastructure lifecycle expose backend capabilities, bounded resources, one total wait budget and explicit task/ISR/startup/destruction contracts without hidden business scheduling.
requirements.acceptance: Actual backend and concurrency tests cover mask/event semantics, nested critical state, clock wrap, exhaustion, stale objects and lifecycle rollback. MCU interrupt/scheduler claims require corresponding physical evidence; unsupported baremetal primitives fail explicitly.

requirements.statement: The platform exposes full physical Flash geometry and generation-checked external regions, while storage and reusable services consume narrow ports without selecting product partitions.
requirements.acceptance: Check density, nonuniform erase blocks, bounds, permissions and region borrowing against production providers. One external layout binds linker and regions; StorageHAL requires compatible geometry and explicit unlock. Fault models recover complete old or new records; physical durability requires real interruption tests.

requirements.statement: External applications and Board packages consume fixed public source SDK targets with explicit composition; SoC, Board and private vendor implementation boundaries remain reviewable.
requirements.acceptance: Build relocated and parent-project consumers through public targets; validate supported Board IRQ/AF/pin resources and reject conflicts. Normal application compilation does not inherit vendor headers or implicit Product policy. Physical Board claims bind actual PCB and measurements; source package checks do not promise a binary ABI.

requirements.statement: Cryptography and update mechanisms use explicit provider and policy ports and return unsupported or failure when required capabilities are absent.
requirements.acceptance: Production core tests reject unconfigured or partial providers, malformed/tampered records and failed update decisions without enabling an implicit backend. MCU keys, entropy, boot policy and trust roots remain external inputs; their hardware qualification requires independently bound evidence.

requirements.statement: Artifact and HIL tooling binds actual source, dependencies, configuration, Board/layout, toolchain and executed results while separating software models from physical qualification.
requirements.acceptance: Reject zero/skipped or mismatched tests, changed artifacts, invalid identities and synthetic physical-HIL claims. A qualified platform claim includes executed board/probe/readback and reviewed resource/timing evidence; tooling consistency alone never promotes qualification.

requirements.statement: The maintained platform states versioned public source compatibility, reviewed architecture changes and accountable maintenance scope without inventing team assignments, enterprise support or LTS.
requirements.acceptance: Current decisions, support matrix and execution record distinguish implemented software, outstanding capabilities and qualification. Public interface changes update callers and meaningful regression records; SDK revision changes remain independently reviewable. Actual reviewer assignments and support commitments require explicit operational evidence.
